description: Manages Registry preference items inside a GPO using Set-GPPrefRegistryValue, Get-GPPrefRegistryValue, and Remove-GPPrefRegistryValue. Unlike policy settings, preference items support Create/Replace/Update/Delete actions and any registry hive.

gpoName.description: Display name of the GPO that contains the Registry preference item.

context.description: 'User' targets User Configuration; 'Computer' targets Computer Configuration.

key.description: Registry key path. Supports HKCR, HKCU, HKLM, HKU, and HKCC (or their full equivalents). Any hive can appear under both User and Computer contexts.

valueName.description: Registry value name. Omit to manage a key-level preference item (no value data).

action.description: Preference action applied on the client: Create, Replace, Update, or Delete. Required when ensure is 'Present'.

type.description: Registry value data type. Required when managing a value (not a key-only item).

value.description: Registry value data. Use a string for String/ExpandString, integer for DWord/QWord, array of strings for MultiString, and a Base64-encoded string for Binary (a legacy array of bytes is also accepted as input).

order.description: Processing order of the preference item within the GPO. Lower numbers are processed last (higher precedence).

disabled.description: When true, the preference item is created in a disabled state and is not applied on the client.

domain.description: FQDN of the domain containing the GPO. Defaults to the current user's domain.

server.description: FQDN or host name of the domain controller to contact. Defaults to the PDC emulator.

ensure.description: 'Present' configures the preference item; 'Absent' removes all matching preference items from the GPO. Defaults to 'Present'.

_exist.description: Whether the preference item should exist. Deprecated — use 'ensure' instead.

disabledDirectly.description: Whether the preference item is directly disabled in the GPO (populated by get/test/set).

_inDesiredState.description: Indicates whether the current state matches the desired state (populated by test/set).
